# STORAGE — where every file lives

Read this before you save, move, back up, or copy any file. One rule set for every agent
(Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) on every machine. Decided by Eric 2026-10-16.

## The model

Every file has one **true copy**. Edit the true copy, or a working copy that syncs back to it
the same day. Everything else is a **backup** (machine-written, never edited) or **scratch**
(thrown away).

Drive is the one place Eric looks. Documents live there directly. Code lives in GitHub and is
mirrored into Drive, so Drive still shows everything.

## Where things go

| What you are saving | True copy | Work on it at | Gets back to the true copy by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet for humans | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`, filed by its `README.md` ladder | Drive desktop app, or `~/DEV/_DRIVE` | Drive sync (automatic) |
| Finished deliverable from a repo | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>` | made in `<repo>/outputs/` | `closeout` copies it (copy, keep the repo one) |
| Code, scripts, project docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub `erash11/<repo>` | `~/DEV/<repo>` | `git commit` + `git push`, every session |
| Generated output (charts, exports, logs) | `<repo>/outputs/` | same | regenerate from code; gitignore it if large |
| Database (DuckDB, SQLite) | local disk, inside its repo or `~/DEV` | same | nightly `daily-backup.ps1` stages the live DBs (not dated `before`/`backup` copies) into `dev-databases.tgz`, uploaded via `gws` to Drive `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` (since 2026-10-20; one copy, no history) |
| Secrets (`.env`, tokens, keys) | macOS Keychain or local `.env` | same | nowhere else — never in git, Drive, or chat |
| Claude/Codex config, skills, memory | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory` | `~/.claude` | `git push` (daily-backup also pushes) |
| A loose file with no home yet | `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | same | `weekly-review` drains it within 7 days |
| Temporary agent work | the session scratchpad | same | thrown away |

Identifiable athlete health data (`DexaProject`, case reviews like `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`) stays
where it is: local or its one Drive folder. Never push it to GitHub, never paste it into chat or an
external service. A folder with a `CLAUDE.md` saying "local only" is in this class.

## Machine-written copies (backups)

Scripts write to Drive `_MACHINE/`. Humans browse `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`. Nothing lives in both.

- `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` — one-way mirror of `~/DEV`, minus databases, secrets, and regenerable/catalog
  caches (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, `.build`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`).
  Written by `~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py` (07:00 and 17:30).
- `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` — nightly `.tgz` snapshots of `~/.claude/projects`, Codex, Gemini, and LaunchAgents
  uploaded directly by `gws` API (`daily-backup.ps1` `Snapshot-Gws`), plus SSD captures of repo data git does not
  carry from `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`.
- External SSD `CRASHBOX` — second nightly copy when it is plugged in.

Read a backup to restore. Edit only the true copy. To add a path to the backups, add it to
`backup-manifest.json`; a path missing from the manifest is not backed up.

## How agents reach Drive

- Read, list, move, and upload through the API: the `gws` CLI (`gws drive files …`), or the Drive MCP.
  Moves keep file IDs; use `gws drive files update` with `addParents`/`removeParents`.
- The mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`) is for Eric and for `cloud-push.py`. Agent
  reads through it can hang, and its view can lag the server by days. Before trusting the mount,
  compare its folder list with `gws drive files list`.
- `gws --upload` only takes a path inside the current directory: `cd` to the file's folder first.

## Places that are never a destination

Baylor OneDrive, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, and the Drive root. If something lands in one of
these, file it by the table above in the same session.

## Before you finish a session

- Every repo you touched: committed and pushed.
- Every deliverable you made: copied to `03_REPORTS/`.
- Every new top-level folder in `~/DEV`: has a `portfolio.json` row (`new-project` does this).

## Known gaps (2026-10-16)

- The Mac's Drive mount went stale because DriveFS was choked on 68,000+ small files in
  `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, leftover `node_modules`).
  Those folders were trashed on Drive via `gws` and excluded in `cloud-push.py` (cutting the file count
  from 104,945 to ~33,735), and `daily-backup.ps1` now uploads its Drive `.tgz` snapshots, receipt, and
  `RESTORE.md` directly via the `gws` API to `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine`, so a lagging local mount can
  never block nightly backups.
- The nightly 00:30 `gws` uploads fail when the Mac is offline or asleep (all FAILED 2026-10-20 00:05, git pushes failed too); a by-hand run succeeds.
- `cloud-push.py` fails under launchd ("Operation not permitted"); it works when run by hand.
- Windows laptop retired 2026-10-14. If a second machine returns, it follows this same table:
  documents through Drive sync, code through `git pull`/`git push`, never a second true copy.

Background and history: `~/DEV/docs/FILE-ORGANIZATION-PLAN.md`.

1	# File Organization Plan — one home for every file
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** execute task-by-task with `superpowers:executing-plans`.
4	> Steps use `- [ ]` checkboxes. **Never delete. Move or park.** Re-check `git status`
5	> at the moment you act, not from an earlier scan (other sessions commit concurrently).
6	
7	**Written:** 2026-10-14 (Mac, Fable). **Owner:** Eric. **Lives here** so both machines see it.
8	
9	**Goal:** Every file has exactly one canonical path. Copies from the Windows era are
10	drained into that path or parked, dated, in one place. New agentic output lands by rule,
11	not by choice.
12	
13	**Architecture:** Two layers, not one.
14	
15	| Layer | Path | Holds | Whose domain | Truth |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| **Code & projects** | `~/DEV/<Area>/<Project>/` | repos, scripts, data pipelines, STATUS.md | agent | git (`erash11`) |
18	| **Documents & deliverables** | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/` (`~/DEV/_DRIVE` symlink) | finished PDFs, decks, admin docs, athlete data for humans | Eric | the stage ladder in its `README.md` |
19	
20	Everything else on disk and on Drive root is a **copy to drain, then park.**
21	
22	**Standing rules now live in `~/.claude/STORAGE.md`** (2026-10-16). This file is the history and the task list.
23	
24	**Spec:** this file is the spec. The Drive ladder is `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/README.md`
25	(2026-08-18) — adopt it, do not redesign it.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Why the last attempt stalled (and what is different now)
30	
31	`MIGRATION_MAP.md` (2026-08-18) built the target folders and said "Nothing has moved yet."
32	Two months later it still has not. Causes, from the record:
33	
34	1. Two machines writing at once → nobody could be sure which copy was current.
35	2. Drive moves through Finder/FUSE are slow and hang (`project_drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop`).
36	3. The first step was "move 13 projects." Too big to finish in one sitting, so it never started.
37	
38	What changed: the Windows laptop is **hands-off since 2026-10-08** (Mac is sole writer), the
39	Google Drive MCP does server-side moves (no FUSE), and this plan's Task 1 finishes in one
40	session and touches nothing you care about.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## What an optimal system looks like for me (the agent)
45	
46	You asked. Concretely:
47	
48	1. **One canonical path per thing.** Duplicates are my real cost. When `memsearch` or
49	   `grep` returns three copies of `report.py`, I cannot tell which is true. I may edit
50	   the wrong one. Every duplicate is a wasted tool call plus a chance to corrupt the right copy.
51	2. **Predictable paths.** If `~/DEV/Performance/VALD_analytics/docs/STATUS.md` always
52	   exists, I go straight there. No search. Search is my fallback, not my front door.
53	3. **One registry, machine-readable.** `project-triage/portfolio.json` + KeystoneOS already
54	   do this. Every folder in `~/DEV` must have a row. A folder with no row is invisible to me.
55	4. **Folder = stage, filename = subject.** The Drive README got this right. Stage has one
56	   answer. Subject has many. I pick folders the same way you do: stop at the first "yes."
57	5. **Short, stable names, no dates in folder names.** `2025-11-25_EOS_Football_Analysis_GPS_ERR`
58	   breaks tab-completion and breaks my memory of the path. Dates belong in `docs/STATUS.md`.
59	6. **Text over binary.** `.md`, `.csv`, `.json` I can read and diff. `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.zip`
60	   I must unpack. Keep binaries as deliverables in `03_REPORTS/`; keep the source as text in the repo.
61	7. **One inbox, one drain rule.** `_INBOX` is fine. An inbox with no weekly drain is a second archive.
62	
63	So: disorganization **does** matter to me. It costs tokens, time, and wrong-copy edits.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Global constraints (never break these)
68	
69	- `~/DEV/.gitignore` starts with `/*`. **Never remove it.** Add `!` exceptions only.
70	- `DexaProject` stays on Drive, never in `~/DEV`, never pasted anywhere.
71	- DuckDB / SQLite files never on Drive (sync locks). DBs and secrets stay local, out of `Cloud_Copy`.
72	- **Never Baylor OneDrive** as a destination. `~/OneDrive - Baylor University` is read-only source.
73	- Windows copies are **read-only sources** to drain. Windows is not a sync peer any more.
74	- **Do not move anything under `~/DEV/Football/` or any live GPS / Perch / VALD pipeline until
75	  the season ends.** It is mid-October. Mid-season work does not get touched.
76	- KeystoneOS discovery is `maxDepth 2`. `DEV/Area/Project` is visible. `DEV/Area/Sub/Project` is not.
77	- Every move: `git status` clean → move → update `portfolio.json` (with provenance) → update the
78	  router `.md` in the same turn → re-run discovery.
79	- No inline Drive scans with `find`. They hang. Use the Drive MCP or a background script.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Inventory of copies (2026-10-14)
84	
85	### Local (Mac)
86	
87	| Path | Size | What it is | Fate |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| `~/DEV_backup_2026-09-09.zip` | 11G | pre-GitHub-consolidation DEV snapshot | hash-diff → park |
90	| `~/Restore/work-laptop-2026-10-08/` | 14G | Windows laptop pull, 10/8 | hash-diff → park |
91	| `~/Restore/_zips/` | (in 14G) | zips from the same pull | hash-diff → park |
92	| `~/handoff-staging/` | 2.7G | `launchd/`, `mac-backup-2026-10-08/`, `merge-losers/` | hash-diff → park |
93	| `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/` | 760M | 41 `gh repo archive`d repos (STATUS: delete after 11/2) | keep until 11/2, then park (last in Task 2) |
94	| `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/` | 4.3G | parked **projects** (canonical, indexed) | keep; projects only, never copies |
95	| `~/_PARKED_COPIES/` | (new) | where drained copies go; outside DEV so backups skip it | the park |
96	| `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | 7.6M | own repo, loose root files | keep; add weekly drain |
97	| `~/OneDrive - Baylor University/` | ? | local OneDrive mirror incl. a second `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` | hash-diff → park; never write |
98	| `~/LindaICE.pdf`, `~/package-lock.json`, `~/restore*.log`, `~/restore.command` | small | root clutter | move to `_INBOX` |
99	
100	### Drive root (`My Drive/`)
101	
102	| Folder | Files | Fate |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `_FROM_WORK_LAPTOP/` | 1,934 | **parked 10-14** → `10_ARCHIVE/_PARKED_COPIES/` (whole; the laptop's final export, 42 zips / 33 GB) |
105	| `OneDrive-Import/` | 41,714 | **parked 10-14** → `10_ARCHIVE/_PARKED_COPIES/` (whole; 1,485 unmatched, filed later by ladder) |
106	| `Backups/` | 9,716 | **KEEP — live.** Nightly target of `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (`Machine/_receipts`, `claude-projects` written 10-14). Not a copy. |
107	| `Mark for deletion/` | 303 | Eric decides (open since 10/3) → park |
108	| `Fireflies Meetings/` | 1,298 | **keep** — pipeline target |
109	| `Zotero_PDFs/` | 314 | **keep** — Zotero storage |
110	| `Claude-Sync-Setup/`, `NewCred/`, `Sports Science Sheets/`, `PFF Weekly Exports/` | tiny | `NewCred` Eric decides; rest → `05_SYSTEMS/` or park |
111	| loose root files (`.gdoc`, `.md`, `.zip`, `.gsheet`) | ~8 | file by ladder → `03_REPORTS/` or `11_PERSONAL/` |
112	
113	### Inside Primary (`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`)
114	
115	`Cloud_Copy/` (the approved daily DEV copy — keep), `athlete-snapshots/`, `pff-snapshots/`
116	(pipeline outputs — keep, move under `05_SYSTEMS/` later), `00_INBOX/` (12 items),
117	`SSAC25_Shapiro_PercentCashWasted_NFL/`, `Transactions-348-2026-02-01.csv` → file by ladder.
118	
119	**`99_UNSORTED/` holds 22,941 files, 23.8 GB** (names-only diff 2026-10-14, after excluding it from
120	the index so it could not match itself): **19,302 have no name+size match anywhere** — `From_Desktop`
121	17,552 files / 19.3 GB, `From_DropBox` 1,191, `From_REMOTE_DESK` 167 / 1.9 GB, `From_GPS_Laptop` 93,
122	`From_GoogleDrive_notsynced` 214, `From_External` 36, `_LongPath_Recovered` 24. This is the dump of every
123	old machine. It is **not a copy to park; it is Task 5 filing work** (ladder, by folder, `From_Desktop` last).
124	Caveat: the index excludes `02_SPORTS/.../02_Raw_Tagging` (Drive hangs listing it), so any face images
125	duplicated there count as unmatched here. Treat 19,302 as an upper bound, not an exact count.
126	Report: `_INBOX/drain-reports/99_UNSORTED.csv`. Other Primary counts for scale: `10_ARCHIVE` 20,000+, `11_PERSONAL` 10,745,
127	`09_PRO_DEV` 8,773, `05_SYSTEMS` 7,306, `04_RESEARCH` 4,266, `03_REPORTS` only 72.
128	
129	### Duplicate clusters inside `~/DEV` (resolve by hand, Task 3)
130	
131	| Cluster | Folders | Likely answer |
132	|---|---|---|
133	| Linda | ~~`Linda Projects`~~, `Linda_Projects` | **done 10-14**: identical (same HEAD 031f96a); space twin parked at `~/_PARKED_COPIES/DEV-twin-checkouts/`; manifest + PROGRAM.md updated |
134	| Body weight | `BodWeightWeb`, `BodyWeightWebApp`, `2026-3-18_BodyWeightNorms` | one app + one norms data repo |
135	| VALD | `VALD_analytics`, `VALD_Performance`, `VALD_Release`, `ValdReport` | one pipeline, one report repo |
136	| Software/Tech | `SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, `SoftwareTech_Review`, `SoftwareTechDocs` | `Review` is live (ET by 11/30); others → merge or park |
137	| Website | `Website`, `WashingtonWebPage`, ~~`AppliedPerformance-Site`~~ | **10-14**: `AppliedPerformance-Site` was a second checkout of the same repo as `Website` (HEAD 873db3d) → parked; `Website` survives (holds the local scroll-craft build). `WashingtonWebPage` (4 files) still Eric's call |
138	| Jump | `Jump_Dash`, `JumpReporting`, `shiny-vertical-jump`, `cmj-norms-app`, `cmj-traffic-light` | check `portfolio.json` `parent` family |
139	
140	---
141	
142	## Review focus (things that bite if unchecked)
143	
144	1. A copy holds a file **newer** than canonical (edited on Windows after the last sync).
145	   The hash-diff must report `copy_mtime > canonical_mtime` on name matches, not just "missing."
146	2. `.from-windows` sidecars (246 of them, per `WINDOWS-SYNC.md`) still exist in repos → they are
147	   duplicates inside canonical. Task 3 sweeps them.
148	3. A project moved into an Area folder whose `.gitignore` covers the whole subtree → silent
149	   backup loss (the 2026-07-28 trap). Check `git check-ignore -v <new path>` after every move.
150	4. `backup-manifest.json` paths break when a repo moves. Update it in the same turn.
151	5. Drive MCP moves change file IDs for `.gdoc` links shared with staff. Move native Google docs
152	   last, and only ones not shared.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## Task 1: Hash-diff every copy against canonical (zero risk, finishes today)
157	
158	**Files:**
159	- Create: `~/DEV/_INBOX/tools/drain_diff.py`
160	- Output: `~/DEV/_INBOX/drain-reports/<copy-name>.csv`
161	
162	**What it does.** Builds one index of canonical: `~/DEV` **and `~/.claude`** by sha256, Primary by
163	`(basename, size)` only (no Drive reads — Drive hangs). `~/.claude` was added 2026-10-14 after the
164	first run showed two copies were mostly old harness folders (plugins, memory, sessions) that the
165	DEV-only index wrongly called "uncovered." `~/.claude/jobs` (per-job temp) is skipped. Then for each copy, lists files that have no match.
166	Zips are read in place with `zipfile`, no extraction.
167	
168	- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script**
169	
170	```python
171	#!/usr/bin/env python3
172	"""drain_diff.py — list files in a copy that are NOT already in canonical.
173	
174	Canonical = ~/DEV (matched by sha256) + Primary Drive (matched by basename+size; never read).
175	Copies can be a directory or a .zip. Never writes outside _INBOX/drain-reports.
176	
177	Usage:
178	  python3 -I drain_diff.py build-index
179	  python3 -I drain_diff.py diff <copy-path> [<copy-path> ...]
180	"""
181	import csv, hashlib, json, os, sys, zipfile
182	from pathlib import Path
183	
184	HOME = Path.home()
185	DEV = HOME / "DEV"
186	PRIMARY = HOME / "Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive"
187	REPORTS = DEV / "_INBOX/drain-reports"
188	INDEX = REPORTS / "canonical-index.json"
189	SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "renv", ".Rproj.user",
190	             "DexaProject"}               # identifiable health data: never indexed, never in a report
191	SKIP_PREFIXES = (str(DEV / "_DRIVE"), str(PRIMARY / "Cloud_Copy"), str(HOME / "_PARKED_COPIES"))
192	ERRORS = 0
193	
194	def sha256(path, bufsize=1 << 20):
195	    h = hashlib.sha256()
196	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
197	        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(bufsize), b""):
198	            h.update(chunk)
199	    return h.hexdigest()
200	
201	def walk(root):
202	    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
203	        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
204	        if dirpath.startswith(SKIP_PREFIXES):
205	            dirnames[:] = []
206	            continue
207	        for fn in filenames:
208	            p = Path(dirpath) / fn
209	            if p.is_symlink():
210	                continue
211	            yield p
212	
213	def build_index(skip_primary=False):
214	    REPORTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
215	    by_hash, by_name_size = {}, {}
216	    n = 0
217	    for p in walk(DEV):
218	        try:
219	            st = p.stat()
220	            by_hash.setdefault(sha256(p), str(p))
221	            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
222	            n += 1
223	        except OSError:
224	            pass
225	    print(f"DEV indexed: {n} files", flush=True)
226	    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
227	    print(f"wrote DEV-only index {INDEX}", flush=True)   # usable even if the Drive walk hangs
228	    if skip_primary:
229	        return
230	    m = 0
231	    for p in walk(PRIMARY):          # stat only; never open Drive files
232	        try:
233	            st = p.stat()
234	            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
235	            m += 1
236	            if m % 2000 == 0:
237	                print(f"  primary: {m} ...", flush=True)
238	        except OSError:
239	            pass
240	    print(f"Primary indexed (name+size): {m} files")
241	    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
242	    print(f"wrote full index {INDEX}")
243	
244	def iter_copy(copy):
245	    """Yield (relative_path, basename, size, sha256, mtime_or_None). Counts unreadable files."""
246	    global ERRORS
247	    copy = Path(copy)
248	    if copy.suffix == ".zip":
249	        with zipfile.ZipFile(copy) as z:
250	            for info in z.infolist():
251	                if info.is_dir() or any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in info.filename.split("/")):
252	                    continue
253	                with z.open(info) as f:
254	                    h = hashlib.sha256()
255	                    for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
256	                        h.update(chunk)
257	                yield info.filename, Path(info.filename).name, info.file_size, h.hexdigest(), None
258	    else:
259	        for p in walk(copy):
260	            try:
261	                st = p.stat()
262	                yield str(p.relative_to(copy)), p.name, st.st_size, sha256(p), st.st_mtime
263	            except OSError:
264	                ERRORS += 1                       # OneDrive placeholders etc.: counted, not hidden
265	
266	def diff(copies):
267	    global ERRORS
268	    idx = json.loads(INDEX.read_text())
269	    by_hash, by_ns = idx["by_hash"], idx["by_name_size"]
270	    by_name = {k.rsplit("|", 1)[0]: v for k, v in by_ns.items()}   # built once: O(1) lookups
271	    for copy in copies:
272	        ERRORS = 0
273	        name = Path(copy).name.replace(".zip", "-zip")
274	        out = REPORTS / f"{name}.csv"
275	        uncovered = newer = total = 0
276	        with open(out, "w", newline="") as fh:
277	            w = csv.writer(fh)
278	            w.writerow(["status", "copy_root", "relative_path", "size", "canonical_match"])
279	            for rel, base, size, h, mtime in iter_copy(copy):
280	                total += 1
281	                if h in by_hash:
282	                    continue                      # byte-identical: covered
283	                if f"{base}|{size}" in by_ns:
284	                    continue                      # same name+size: covered
285	                match = by_name.get(base, "")
286	                status = "UNCOVERED"
287	                if match and mtime:
288	                    try:
289	                        if mtime > Path(match).stat().st_mtime:
290	                            status, newer = "NEWER_THAN_CANONICAL", newer + 1
291	                    except OSError:
292	                        pass
293	                uncovered += 1
294	                w.writerow([status, str(copy), rel, size, match])
295	        print(f"{copy}: {total} files, {uncovered} uncovered ({newer} newer than canonical), "
296	              f"{ERRORS} unreadable -> {out}", flush=True)
297	
298	if __name__ == "__main__":
299	    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
300	    if cmd == "build-index":
301	        build_index(skip_primary="--skip-primary" in sys.argv)
302	    elif cmd == "diff" and len(sys.argv) > 2:
303	        diff(sys.argv[2:])
304	    else:
305	        print(__doc__); sys.exit(2)
306	```

# File Organization Plan — one home for every file

> **For agentic workers:** execute task-by-task with `superpowers:executing-plans`.
> Steps use `- [ ]` checkboxes. **Never delete. Move or park.** Re-check `git status`
> at the moment you act, not from an earlier scan (other sessions commit concurrently).

**Written:** 2026-10-14 (Mac, Fable). **Owner:** Eric. **Lives here** so both machines see it.

**Goal:** Every file has exactly one canonical path. Copies from the Windows era are
drained into that path or parked, dated, in one place. New agentic output lands by rule,
not by choice.

**Architecture:** Two layers, not one.

| Layer | Path | Holds | Whose domain | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Code & projects** | `~/DEV/<Area>/<Project>/` | repos, scripts, data pipelines, STATUS.md | agent | git (`erash11`) |
| **Documents & deliverables** | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/` (`~/DEV/_DRIVE` symlink) | finished PDFs, decks, admin docs, athlete data for humans | Eric | the stage ladder in its `README.md` |

Everything else on disk and on Drive root is a **copy to drain, then park.**

**Standing rules now live in `~/.claude/STORAGE.md`** (2026-10-16). This file is the history and the task list.

**Spec:** this file is the spec. The Drive ladder is `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/README.md`

## What an optimal system looks like for me (the agent)

You asked. Concretely:

1. **One canonical path per thing.** Duplicates are my real cost. When `memsearch` or
   `grep` returns three copies of `report.py`, I cannot tell which is true. I may edit
   the wrong one. Every duplicate is a wasted tool call plus a chance to corrupt the right copy.
2. **Predictable paths.** If `~/DEV/Performance/VALD_analytics/docs/STATUS.md` always
   exists, I go straight there. No search. Search is my fallback, not my front door.
3. **One registry, machine-readable.** `project-triage/portfolio.json` + KeystoneOS already
   do this. Every folder in `~/DEV` must have a row. A folder with no row is invisible to me.
4. **Folder = stage, filename = subject.** The Drive README got this right. Stage has one
   answer. Subject has many. I pick folders the same way you do: stop at the first "yes."
5. **Short, stable names, no dates in folder names.** `2025-11-25_EOS_Football_Analysis_GPS_ERR`
   breaks tab-completion and breaks my memory of the path. Dates belong in `docs/STATUS.md`.
6. **Text over binary.** `.md`, `.csv`, `.json` I can read and diff. `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.zip`
   I must unpack. Keep binaries as deliverables in `03_REPORTS/`; keep the source as text in the repo.
7. **One inbox, one drain rule.** `_INBOX` is fine. An inbox with no weekly drain is a second archive.

So: disorganization **does** matter to me. It costs tokens, time, and wrong-copy edits.

## Task 1: Hash-diff every copy against canonical (zero risk, finishes today)

**Files:**
- Create: `~/DEV/_INBOX/tools/drain_diff.py`
- Output: `~/DEV/_INBOX/drain-reports/<copy-name>.csv`

**What it does.** Builds one index of canonical: `~/DEV` **and `~/.claude`** by sha256, Primary by
`(basename, size)` only (no Drive reads — Drive hangs). `~/.claude` was added 2026-10-14 after the
first run showed two copies were mostly old harness folders (plugins, memory, sessions) that the
DEV-only index wrongly called "uncovered." `~/.claude/jobs` (per-job temp) is skipped. Then for each copy, lists files that have no match.
Zips are read in place with `zipfile`, no extraction.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""drain_diff.py — list files in a copy that are NOT already in canonical.

Canonical = ~/DEV (matched by sha256) + Primary Drive (matched by basename+size; never read).
Copies can be a directory or a .zip. Never writes outside _INBOX/drain-reports.

Usage:
  python3 -I drain_diff.py build-index
  python3 -I drain_diff.py diff <copy-path> [<copy-path> ...]
"""
import csv, hashlib, json, os, sys, zipfile
from pathlib import Path

HOME = Path.home()
DEV = HOME / "DEV"
PRIMARY = HOME / "Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive"
REPORTS = DEV / "_INBOX/drain-reports"
INDEX = REPORTS / "canonical-index.json"
SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "renv", ".Rproj.user",
             "DexaProject"}               # identifiable health data: never indexed, never in a report
SKIP_PREFIXES = (str(DEV / "_DRIVE"), str(PRIMARY / "Cloud_Copy"), str(HOME / "_PARKED_COPIES"))
ERRORS = 0

def sha256(path, bufsize=1 << 20):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(bufsize), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()

def walk(root):
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        if dirpath.startswith(SKIP_PREFIXES):
            dirnames[:] = []
            continue
        for fn in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / fn
            if p.is_symlink():
                continue
            yield p

def build_index(skip_primary=False):
    REPORTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    by_hash, by_name_size = {}, {}
    n = 0
    for p in walk(DEV):
        try:
            st = p.stat()
            by_hash.setdefault(sha256(p), str(p))
            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
            n += 1
        except OSError:
            pass
    print(f"DEV indexed: {n} files", flush=True)
    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
    print(f"wrote DEV-only index {INDEX}", flush=True)   # usable even if the Drive walk hangs
    if skip_primary:
        return
    m = 0
    for p in walk(PRIMARY):          # stat only; never open Drive files
        try:
            st = p.stat()
            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
            m += 1
            if m % 2000 == 0:
                print(f"  primary: {m} ...", flush=True)
        except OSError:
            pass
    print(f"Primary indexed (name+size): {m} files")
    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
    print(f"wrote full index {INDEX}")

def iter_copy(copy):
    """Yield (relative_path, basename, size, sha256, mtime_or_None). Counts unreadable files."""
    global ERRORS
    copy = Path(copy)
    if copy.suffix == ".zip":
        with zipfile.ZipFile(copy) as z:
            for info in z.infolist():
                if info.is_dir() or any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in info.filename.split("/")):
                    continue
                with z.open(info) as f:
                    h = hashlib.sha256()
                    for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
                        h.update(chunk)
                yield info.filename, Path(info.filename).name, info.file_size, h.hexdigest(), None
    else:
        for p in walk(copy):
            try:
                st = p.stat()
                yield str(p.relative_to(copy)), p.name, st.st_size, sha256(p), st.st_mtime
            except OSError:
                ERRORS += 1                       # OneDrive placeholders etc.: counted, not hidden

def diff(copies):
    global ERRORS
    idx = json.loads(INDEX.read_text())
    by_hash, by_ns = idx["by_hash"], idx["by_name_size"]
    by_name = {k.rsplit("|", 1)[0]: v for k, v in by_ns.items()}   # built once: O(1) lookups
    for copy in copies:
        ERRORS = 0
        name = Path(copy).name.replace(".zip", "-zip")
        out = REPORTS / f"{name}.csv"
        uncovered = newer = total = 0
        with open(out, "w", newline="") as fh:
            w = csv.writer(fh)
            w.writerow(["status", "copy_root", "relative_path", "size", "canonical_match"])
            for rel, base, size, h, mtime in iter_copy(copy):
                total += 1
                if h in by_hash:
                    continue                      # byte-identical: covered
                if f"{base}|{size}" in by_ns:
                    continue                      # same name+size: covered
                match = by_name.get(base, "")
                status = "UNCOVERED"
                if match and mtime:
                    try:
                        if mtime > Path(match).stat().st_mtime:
                            status, newer = "NEWER_THAN_CANONICAL", newer + 1
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                uncovered += 1
                w.writerow([status, str(copy), rel, size, match])
        print(f"{copy}: {total} files, {uncovered} uncovered ({newer} newer than canonical), "
              f"{ERRORS} unreadable -> {out}", flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
    if cmd == "build-index":
        build_index(skip_primary="--skip-primary" in sys.argv)
    elif cmd == "diff" and len(sys.argv) > 2:
        diff(sys.argv[2:])
    else:
        print(__doc__); sys.exit(2)
```

1	# STORAGE — where every file lives
2	
3	Read this before you save, move, back up, or copy any file. One rule set for every agent
4	(Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) on every machine. Decided by Eric 2026-10-16.
5	
6	## The model
7	
8	Every file has one **true copy**. Edit the true copy, or a working copy that syncs back to it
9	the same day. Everything else is a **backup** (machine-written, never edited) or **scratch**
10	(thrown away).
11	
12	Drive is the one place Eric looks. Documents live there directly. Code lives in GitHub and is
13	mirrored into Drive, so Drive still shows everything.
14	
15	## Where things go
16	
17	| What you are saving | True copy | Work on it at | Gets back to the true copy by |
18	|---|---|---|---|
19	| Document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet for humans | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`, filed by its `README.md` ladder | Drive desktop app, or `~/DEV/_DRIVE` | Drive sync (automatic) |
20	| Finished deliverable from a repo | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>` | made in `<repo>/outputs/` | `closeout` copies it (copy, keep the repo one) |
21	| Code, scripts, project docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub `erash11/<repo>` | `~/DEV/<repo>` | `git commit` + `git push`, every session |
22	| Generated output (charts, exports, logs) | `<repo>/outputs/` | same | regenerate from code; gitignore it if large |
23	| Database (DuckDB, SQLite) | local disk, inside its repo or `~/DEV` | same | nightly `daily-backup.ps1` stages the live DBs (not dated `before`/`backup` copies) into `dev-databases.tgz`, uploaded via `gws` to Drive `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` (since 2026-10-20; one copy, no history) |
24	| Secrets (`.env`, tokens, keys) | macOS Keychain or local `.env` | same | nowhere else — never in git, Drive, or chat |
25	| Claude/Codex config, skills, memory | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory` | `~/.claude` | `git push` (daily-backup also pushes) |
26	| A loose file with no home yet | `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | same | `weekly-review` drains it within 7 days |
27	| Temporary agent work | the session scratchpad | same | thrown away |
28	
29	Identifiable athlete health data (`DexaProject`, case reviews like `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`) stays
30	where it is: local or its one Drive folder. Never push it to GitHub, never paste it into chat or an
31	external service. A folder with a `CLAUDE.md` saying "local only" is in this class.
32	
33	## Machine-written copies (backups)
34	
35	Scripts write to Drive `_MACHINE/`. Humans browse `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`. Nothing lives in both.
36	
37	- `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` — one-way mirror of `~/DEV`, minus databases, secrets, and regenerable/catalog
38	  caches (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, `.build`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`).
39	  Written by `~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py` (07:00 and 17:30).
40	- `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` — nightly `.tgz` snapshots of `~/.claude/projects`, Codex, Gemini, and LaunchAgents
41	  uploaded directly by `gws` API (`daily-backup.ps1` `Snapshot-Gws`), plus SSD captures of repo data git does not
42	  carry from `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`.
43	- External SSD `CRASHBOX` — second nightly copy when it is plugged in.
44	
45	Read a backup to restore. Edit only the true copy. To add a path to the backups, add it to
46	`backup-manifest.json`; a path missing from the manifest is not backed up.
47	
48	## How agents reach Drive
49	
50	- Read, list, move, and upload through the API: the `gws` CLI (`gws drive files …`), or the Drive MCP.
51	  Moves keep file IDs; use `gws drive files update` with `addParents`/`removeParents`.
52	- The mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`) is for Eric and for `cloud-push.py`. Agent
53	  reads through it can hang, and its view can lag the server by days. Before trusting the mount,
54	  compare its folder list with `gws drive files list`.
55	- `gws --upload` only takes a path inside the current directory: `cd` to the file's folder first.
56	
57	## Places that are never a destination
58	
59	Baylor OneDrive, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, and the Drive root. If something lands in one of
60	these, file it by the table above in the same session.
61	
62	## Before you finish a session

64	- Every repo you touched: committed and pushed.
65	- Every deliverable you made: copied to `03_REPORTS/`.
66	- Every new top-level folder in `~/DEV`: has a `portfolio.json` row (`new-project` does this).

164	first run showed two copies were mostly old harness folders (plugins, memory, sessions) that the
165	DEV-only index wrongly called "uncovered." `~/.claude/jobs` (per-job temp) is skipped. Then for each copy, lists files that have no match.
166	Zips are read in place with `zipfile`, no extraction.
167	
168	- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script**
169	
170	```python
171	#!/usr/bin/env python3
172	"""drain_diff.py — list files in a copy that are NOT already in canonical.
173	
174	Canonical = ~/DEV (matched by sha256) + Primary Drive (matched by basename+size; never read).
175	Copies can be a directory or a .zip. Never writes outside _INBOX/drain-reports.
176	
177	Usage:
178	  python3 -I drain_diff.py build-index
179	  python3 -I drain_diff.py diff <copy-path> [<copy-path> ...]
180	"""
181	import csv, hashlib, json, os, sys, zipfile
182	from pathlib import Path
183	
184	HOME = Path.home()
185	DEV = HOME / "DEV"
186	PRIMARY = HOME / "Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive"
187	REPORTS = DEV / "_INBOX/drain-reports"
188	INDEX = REPORTS / "canonical-index.json"
189	SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "renv", ".Rproj.user",
190	             "DexaProject"}               # identifiable health data: never indexed, never in a report
191	SKIP_PREFIXES = (str(DEV / "_DRIVE"), str(PRIMARY / "Cloud_Copy"), str(HOME / "_PARKED_COPIES"))
192	ERRORS = 0
193	
194	def sha256(path, bufsize=1 << 20):
195	    h = hashlib.sha256()
196	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
197	        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(bufsize), b""):
198	            h.update(chunk)
199	    return h.hexdigest()
200	
201	def walk(root):
202	    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
203	        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
204	        if dirpath.startswith(SKIP_PREFIXES):
205	            dirnames[:] = []
206	            continue
207	        for fn in filenames:
208	            p = Path(dirpath) / fn
209	            if p.is_symlink():
210	                continue
211	            yield p
212	
213	def build_index(skip_primary=False):
214	    REPORTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
215	    by_hash, by_name_size = {}, {}
216	    n = 0
217	    for p in walk(DEV):
218	        try:
219	            st = p.stat()
220	            by_hash.setdefault(sha256(p), str(p))
221	            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
222	            n += 1
223	        except OSError:
224	            pass
225	    print(f"DEV indexed: {n} files", flush=True)
226	    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
227	    print(f"wrote DEV-only index {INDEX}", flush=True)   # usable even if the Drive walk hangs
228	    if skip_primary:
229	        return
230	    m = 0
231	    for p in walk(PRIMARY):          # stat only; never open Drive files
232	        try:
233	            st = p.stat()
234	            by_name_size.setdefault(f"{p.name}|{st.st_size}", str(p))
235	            m += 1
236	            if m % 2000 == 0:
237	                print(f"  primary: {m} ...", flush=True)
238	        except OSError:
239	            pass
240	    print(f"Primary indexed (name+size): {m} files")
241	    INDEX.write_text(json.dumps({"by_hash": by_hash, "by_name_size": by_name_size}))
242	    print(f"wrote full index {INDEX}")
243	
244	def iter_copy(copy):
245	    """Yield (relative_path, basename, size, sha256, mtime_or_None). Counts unreadable files."""
246	    global ERRORS
247	    copy = Path(copy)
248	    if copy.suffix == ".zip":
249	        with zipfile.ZipFile(copy) as z:
250	            for info in z.infolist():
251	                if info.is_dir() or any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in info.filename.split("/")):
252	                    continue
253	                with z.open(info) as f:
254	                    h = hashlib.sha256()
255	                    for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
256	                        h.update(chunk)
257	                yield info.filename, Path(info.filename).name, info.file_size, h.hexdigest(), None
258	    else:
259	        for p in walk(copy):
260	            try:
261	                st = p.stat()
262	                yield str(p.relative_to(copy)), p.name, st.st_size, sha256(p), st.st_mtime
263	            except OSError:
264	                ERRORS += 1                       # OneDrive placeholders etc.: counted, not hidden
265	
266	def diff(copies):
267	    global ERRORS
268	    idx = json.loads(INDEX.read_text())
269	    by_hash, by_ns = idx["by_hash"], idx["by_name_size"]
270	    by_name = {k.rsplit("|", 1)[0]: v for k, v in by_ns.items()}   # built once: O(1) lookups
271	    for copy in copies:
272	        ERRORS = 0
273	        name = Path(copy).name.replace(".zip", "-zip")
274	        out = REPORTS / f"{name}.csv"
275	        uncovered = newer = total = 0
276	        with open(out, "w", newline="") as fh:
277	            w = csv.writer(fh)
278	            w.writerow(["status", "copy_root", "relative_path", "size", "canonical_match"])
279	            for rel, base, size, h, mtime in iter_copy(copy):
280	                total += 1
281	                if h in by_hash:
282	                    continue                      # byte-identical: covered
283	                if f"{base}|{size}" in by_ns:
284	                    continue                      # same name+size: covered
285	                match = by_name.get(base, "")
286	                status = "UNCOVERED"
287	                if match and mtime:
288	                    try:
289	                        if mtime > Path(match).stat().st_mtime:
290	                            status, newer = "NEWER_THAN_CANONICAL", newer + 1
291	                    except OSError:
292	                        pass
293	                uncovered += 1
294	                w.writerow([status, str(copy), rel, size, match])
295	        print(f"{copy}: {total} files, {uncovered} uncovered ({newer} newer than canonical), "
296	              f"{ERRORS} unreadable -> {out}", flush=True)
297	
298	if __name__ == "__main__":
299	    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
300	    if cmd == "build-index":
301	        build_index(skip_primary="--skip-primary" in sys.argv)
302	    elif cmd == "diff" and len(sys.argv) > 2:
303	        diff(sys.argv[2:])
304	    else:
305	        print(__doc__); sys.exit(2)
306	```

# Flint

Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. The name comes from Proverbs 27:17 ("iron sharpens iron"): the job is to
sharpen Eric's reasoning, not soothe it.

This repo holds the knowledge-ingest project that feeds Flint. It is a **side-lane**
project (outside the prioritization-slate cap, by Eric's choice on 2026-09-26). No
charter. It runs as small background batches during the season.

## The idea

Claude does not learn from files. What makes Flint better is what is stored and
findable: Zotero full text, SecondBrain vault notes, and above all **per-discipline
synthesis notes** that record where the sources agree, where they disagree, and
where Eric lands. So the job is not "ingest everything". It has three layers:

1. **Catalog everything** with a script, spending no tokens (step 0 below).
2. **Deep-ingest a short ranked list.**
3. **Synthesize one discipline at a time.** This layer is the thought partner.

## Steps

| Step | What | Tool | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Manifest + dedup of all sources (metadata only, via the Drive API) | `scripts/build_manifest.ps1` | built 2026-09-26 |
| 1 | Eric's own method: Applied Performance Playbook, AP Assessment Manual V12, HHPR 5355 transcripts, force-plate protocols, Sportsmith articles, plus his written decision rules (via `/interview-me`) | Claude | next |
| 2 | Triage each unique file: discipline + tier (A deep-ingest / B catalog only / C skip) | Haiku + Codex | |
| 3 | Route tier A by type: papers → Zotero (after its 92-item queue clears); courses with transcripts → vault atomization; books → `ingest-book` behind the review gate; video → overnight transcription queue | existing pipelines | |
| 4 | Per-discipline synthesis notes (e.g. hamstring RTP: Harries vs Landon vs TB/David Grey vs Eric's manual) | Claude + Eric review | |

Eric's own material goes first for a structural reason. Every synthesis note compares
a source against how Eric already works, and that comparison is impossible until his
method is in.

## Sources

The roots are listed in `config/roots.json`. To add a source, edit the list; the code
does not change.

- Eric's Drive: 07_EDUCATION, 06_TEMPLATES, SPORT_SCIENCE, 09_PRO_DEV,
  From_REMOTE_DESK (this includes **Landon Evans**, about 800 files), 04_RESEARCH.
- My Drive, outside `00_Primary_Storage_Drive`: **Athletic Performance & Sports
  Science** (Literature & Textbooks, Training Programs & Planners, Coach Lowe's
  material, Seminars & Presentations with Pfaff, Moyer and Korfist), **RTP Clinic —
  Take-Home Resources**, and **Research Papers**. `Zotero_PDFs` is excluded because
  Zotero owns it, and `CATAPULT_HUB_PRO` is excluded because it is athlete data.
- **TB's Training Info**: Thomas Barbeau's shared folder. 2,179 files, 75 GB, about 80
  coaches or systems (SC Books, Stop Chasing Pain, DNS, David Grey Rehab, Burdenko,
  ALTIS, ELDOA, ...). It is **not synced locally** and is still being edited by its
  owner, so snapshot it with `gws` before ingesting.
- Shared folders: the Pro Football Sports Science Research Update issues, the 2026
  CSCCa conference presentations, the Enoka ISB talk, and coach Lowe's drill folders.

## Rules

- **DexaProject, athlete data, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued**
  (`exclude_path_regex`). Spreadsheets and images are kept (Eric lifted the privacy filter 2026-09-26).
- **Codex workers only ever see staged copies**, in a scratch folder, never the Drive
  root. Codex is an external service. Pilot one batch before fanning out.
----
# STATUS

## 2026-10-13 (Mac, closeout): audit of the Ch9 commit
- The 20 extra files in `3f8b5d0` are not new content. 14 are Chapters 1-8 entries; 5 are Chapter 9 entries; `_book.md` is the index. All 19 entries match their vault copies. Nothing needs moving. Handoff: `docs/handoffs/2026-10-13-closeout-ch9-audit.md`.
- Three Chapter 9 entries are in the vault but were never in the Sol 6.1 review: `claim--post-work-protein-synthesis-runs-with-degradation-to-renew-muscle-proteins.md`, `claim--training-specificity-extends-to-hormonal-regulation-of-metabolism.md`, `heuristic--run-short-hills-with-a-forward-take-off-not-half-bent-legs.md`. The folder now has 67 Ch9 entries; 64 were reviewed.

## Current state
- Supertraining 6th ed. Ch8 (97), Ch9 (64) and the missing-ideas follow-up (8 new, 11 cross-links) are in the SecondBrain vault. Staging matches the vault for these files.
- Ingest plan (`docs/INGEST-PLAN.md`) approved on decisions 1 and 2. Step 0, the Drive recount, is not done.

## Next
1. Decide the open question below (default: leave it skipped).
2. Run the Drive recount (step 0 of `docs/INGEST-PLAN.md`) and report the true file counts here.

## Open questions
- Should the three unreviewed Chapter 9 entries (post-work protein synthesis, training specificity, short hills) get a Sol 6.1 falsifying review now, as the 64 did? Default if no answer: leave them as Opus-reviewed only and say so in the Ch9 record. Each needs the same review, fix and lint steps.
- Rehabilitation stages idea (Supertraining PDF 438, p.427): "Rehabilitation must follow the same stages of periodised training as normal training." It was skipped because the return-to-play entry already quotes this sentence, and the reviewer agreed. Should it be its own entry anyway? Default: no.

## Gotchas
- Staging can change under you. Commit 3f8b5d0 (Codex Ch9 fixes, 56 entries) landed in staging after promotion. Check `git status` in the folder before editing.
- Never copy a staging file over a vault file that holds vault-only text. Merge by position instead.
- Lint needs the full staging path, or it checks nothing.

## 2026-10-13 (Mac, close-out): Supertraining outstanding items cleared
- Vault: `f9da60b` (LDTE locator fixes, index dash cleanup). Lint: 0 issues.

- Chapter 8 Codex review (Sol 6.1): 34 fixes already in staging (`856301a`) and in the vault. Chapter 9 Codex review: fixes already in the vault (`8492d48`).
- Open for the vault only: uncommitted changes in `research-papers/`. Not ours.

## 2026-10-13 (Mac, follow-up promoted): Missing-ideas follow-up in the vault

# Consolidation Plan

Status: proposed, not executed. Date: 2026-10-15.

## Target operating model

One authoritative location per retained asset, one clear entry point for each project, and explicit recovery backups. A locally cached cloud file is not an independent working copy; a separately edited backup folder is. The goal is to remove ambiguity and unmanaged copies while retaining recoverability.

Retain the existing Primary structure initially. Avoid bulk renaming or uploading all sources into a new staging tree. Inventory in place, then reconcile one project at a time. Machine configuration backups remain a separate category from project documents and source code.

## Decisions before cutover

| Decision | Options | Planning default, not approval |
|---|---|---|
| Meaning of cloud-first | Drive-based files with local execution; cloud execution; a mixture | Inventory first; select per workload |
| Source code authority | Drive files; existing remote Git repository; future cloud workspace | Inspect current repositories before choosing |
| Local storage | Cloud cache, temporary compute data, or fully local work | No unique retained work should exist only locally after migration |
| Project registry | Existing portfolio registry with cloud visibility; replacement index | Extend existing registry if suitable |
| Retention | User-defined recovery window and backup history | Suggest 30 days for quarantine, subject to approval |

Do not promise reliable cross-platform execution merely because project files are on Drive. Classify dependencies, databases, virtual environments, Git metadata, file locks, absolute paths, and platform-specific binaries. Validate the chosen workflow with a representative project. If proposing Git/cloud execution products, verify current official documentation and get agreement before introducing a service. The user has not selected these options.

## Phase 1 — Complete discovery

1. Enumerate owned My Drive files and relevant shared items with pagination, including computer-backup areas if available. Separate shortcuts from their targets and keep IDs as identity.
2. Inventory the Primary, Cloud_Copy, and Backups trees recursively. Record every skipped/inaccessible area and page continuation. Do not call a 100-item listing complete.
3. On Windows and Mac, identify actual DEV roots, external drives, Drive mounts, and backup folders. First collect metadata; read contents only where comparison needs them. Do not follow symlink/junction loops.
4. Read the discovered sync/migration docs, portfolio registry, and current scripts/configuration. Inspect task scheduler/launch agents read-only. Map each writer's source, destination, schedule, exclusions, and failure reporting.
5. Record local files absent from Drive, cloud files absent locally, and potentially stale cloud snapshots.

Deliverables: complete inventory with coverage report; automation dependency table; project crosswalk; unresolved-access list. Exit condition: each in-scope source is inventoried or explicitly marked unavailable, with no implied coverage of unavailable sources.

## Phase 2 — Compare and classify

Group projects using registry records, repository identity, path relationships, and content evidence. Names are hints only. For each candidate pair:

- Equal strong content hashes and sizes: exact-byte duplicate candidate. Compare ownership, permissions, links, comments, and history before choosing a survivor.
- Same name but different content: version conflict; preserve both until resolved.
- Different names with equal content: possible redundant copy; check contextual need.
- Editable source and PDF/export: related artifacts with different functions, not duplicates.
- Native Google documents: inspect IDs, revisions, contents and collaboration metadata; do not use an exported PDF hash as proof of equivalent originals.
- Repository copies: compare remotes, branches, commits, untracked files and working-tree changes. A newer folder timestamp is not sufficient.
- Backup snapshots: classify under recovery retention; do not merge blindly into active projects.

Deliverable: one row per proposed action with evidence and proposed canonical destination. Unknown/conflicting items receive `review`, never automatic deletion.

## Phase 3 — Define homes and pilot

Create a project map with stable project key, stage, canonical Drive folder ID, any code remote, Windows/Mac working locations, recovery location, automation owner, and last verification date. Inspect the existing portfolio schema first; add a companion map if needed without breaking its consumers.

Select one modest noncritical project with overlapping copies. Confirm unique local work is retained. Prepare a dry-run manifest, rollback instructions, and expected file counts/hashes. Present that concrete pilot for migration authorization. No bulk changes are justified by approval of a single pilot.

## Phase 4 — Execute approved batches

1. Re-read affected file metadata and detect changes since inventory. Abort stale actions.
2. Coordinate a brief editing pause and pause only the identified writers for the batch when authorized. Capture their settings.
3. Preserve a recovery point. Prefer moves within Drive where suitable to preserve IDs; copying creates new IDs and may alter metadata/sharing.
4. Move or reconcile files using the approved manifest. Never overwrite an unresolved conflict.
5. Update path-dependent scripts, shortcuts, application settings, and registry entries together with their destination changes.
6. Verify destination membership, contents, access, application behavior and representative scripts on each intended platform. Record per-action results immediately.
7. Resume the intended writers and verify their next output location. Check that retired trees are not recreated.

On errors: stop the affected batch, retain all unique data, log completed actions, and roll back only verified changes. Do not reverse a move over newly edited content; reconcile it first.

## Phase 5 — Quarantine and retire

After canonical copies are verified, place approved redundant material in a clearly labeled quarantine or otherwise mark it inactive. Preserve original IDs/paths and a restoration manifest. Quarantine relocation can itself affect paths, so it also belongs in the approved batch.

Delete only specifically authorized, verified redundant items after the agreed retention interval. A folder named Mark for deletion does not establish current permission. Permanently deleting recovery data is a separate explicit decision. Retire old jobs and update both existing READMEs to reflect the actual operating model.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every retained project has an agreed authoritative cloud home and registry entry.
- Every available source is inventoried; unavailable sources are disclosed.
- All unique local work has been reconciled or explicitly deferred.
- Duplicate decisions contain content evidence, not just names/dates.
- Both computers can access the intended materials; selected code workflows pass representative execution checks.
- Zotero attachments, Fireflies outputs, and other identified pipelines continue functioning.
- No automation recreates the retired copies during a normal run cycle.
- Recovery restoration is demonstrated for one representative item.
- Updated documentation, manifest, unresolved exceptions and progress log are available in this handoff folder.

## Ongoing upkeep

Use one intake folder, a short weekly filing review, and a documented project closeout step. Keep backups out of everyday project navigation. Use Drive-native shortcuts where a second browsing entry is needed, subject to access checks. Record exceptions rather than forcing all workloads into identical storage behavior.

# Consolidation Plan

Status: proposed, not executed. Date: 2026-10-15.

## Target operating model

One authoritative location per retained asset, one clear entry point for each project, and explicit recovery backups. A locally cached cloud file is not an independent working copy; a separately edited backup folder is. The goal is to remove ambiguity and unmanaged copies while retaining recoverability.

Retain the existing Primary structure initially. Avoid bulk renaming or uploading all sources into a new staging tree. Inventory in place, then reconcile one project at a time. Machine configuration backups remain a separate category from project documents and source code.

## Decisions before cutover

| Decision | Options | Planning default, not approval |
|---|---|---|
| Meaning of cloud-first | Drive-based files with local execution; cloud execution; a mixture | Inventory first; select per workload |
| Source code authority | Drive files; existing remote Git repository; future cloud workspace | Inspect current repositories before choosing |
| Local storage | Cloud cache, temporary compute data, or fully local work | No unique retained work should exist only locally after migration |
| Project registry | Existing portfolio registry with cloud visibility; replacement index | Extend existing registry if suitable |
| Retention | User-defined recovery window and backup history | Suggest 30 days for quarantine, subject to approval |

Do not promise reliable cross-platform execution merely because project files are on Drive. Classify dependencies, databases, virtual environments, Git metadata, file locks, absolute paths, and platform-specific binaries. Validate the chosen workflow with a representative project. If proposing Git/cloud execution products, verify current official documentation and get agreement before introducing a service. The user has not selected these options.

## Phase 1 — Complete discovery

1. Enumerate owned My Drive files and relevant shared items with pagination, including computer-backup areas if available. Separate shortcuts from their targets and keep IDs as identity.
2. Inventory the Primary, Cloud_Copy, and Backups trees recursively. Record every skipped/inaccessible area and page continuation. Do not call a 100-item listing complete.
3. On Windows and Mac, identify actual DEV roots, external drives, Drive mounts, and backup folders. First collect metadata; read contents only where comparison needs them. Do not follow symlink/junction loops.
4. Read the discovered sync/migration docs, portfolio registry, and current scripts/configuration. Inspect task scheduler/launch agents read-only. Map each writer's source, destination, schedule, exclusions, and failure reporting.
5. Record local files absent from Drive, cloud files absent locally, and potentially stale cloud snapshots.

Deliverables: complete inventory with coverage report; automation dependency table; project crosswalk; unresolved-access list. Exit condition: each in-scope source is inventoried or explicitly marked unavailable, with no implied coverage of unavailable sources.

## Phase 2 — Compare and classify

Group projects using registry records, repository identity, path relationships, and content evidence. Names are hints only. For each candidate pair:

- Equal strong content hashes and sizes: exact-byte duplicate candidate. Compare ownership, permissions, links, comments, and history before choosing a survivor.
- Same name but different content: version conflict; preserve both until resolved.
- Different names with equal content: possible redundant copy; check contextual need.
- Editable source and PDF/export: related artifacts with different functions, not duplicates.
- Native Google documents: inspect IDs, revisions, contents and collaboration metadata; do not use an exported PDF hash as proof of equivalent originals.
- Repository copies: compare remotes, branches, commits, untracked files and working-tree changes. A newer folder timestamp is not sufficient.
- Backup snapshots: classify under recovery retention; do not merge blindly into active projects.

Deliverable: one row per proposed action with evidence and proposed canonical destination. Unknown/conflicting items receive `review`, never automatic deletion.

## Phase 3 — Define homes and pilot

Create a project map with stable project key, stage, canonical Drive folder ID, any code remote, Windows/Mac working locations, recovery location, automation owner, and last verification date. Inspect the existing portfolio schema first; add a companion map if needed without breaking its consumers.

Select one modest noncritical project with overlapping copies. Confirm unique local work is retained. Prepare a dry-run manifest, rollback instructions, and expected file counts/hashes. Present that concrete pilot for migration authorization. No bulk changes are justified by approval of a single pilot.

## Phase 4 — Execute approved batches

1. Re-read affected file metadata and detect changes since inventory. Abort stale actions.
2. Coordinate a brief editing pause and pause only the identified writers for the batch when authorized. Capture their settings.
3. Preserve a recovery point. Prefer moves within Drive where suitable to preserve IDs; copying creates new IDs and may alter metadata/sharing.
4. Move or reconcile files using the approved manifest. Never overwrite an unresolved conflict.
5. Update path-dependent scripts, shortcuts, application settings, and registry entries together with their destination changes.
6. Verify destination membership, contents, access, application behavior and representative scripts on each intended platform. Record per-action results immediately.
7. Resume the intended writers and verify their next output location. Check that retired trees are not recreated.

On errors: stop the affected batch, retain all unique data, log completed actions, and roll back only verified changes. Do not reverse a move over newly edited content; reconcile it first.

## Phase 5 — Quarantine and retire

After canonical copies are verified, place approved redundant material in a clearly labeled quarantine or otherwise mark it inactive. Preserve original IDs/paths and a restoration manifest. Quarantine relocation can itself affect paths, so it also belongs in the approved batch.

Delete only specifically authorized, verified redundant items after the agreed retention interval. A folder named Mark for deletion does not establish current permission. Permanently deleting recovery data is a separate explicit decision. Retire old jobs and update both existing READMEs to reflect the actual operating model.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every retained project has an agreed authoritative cloud home and registry entry.
- Every available source is inventoried; unavailable sources are disclosed.
- All unique local work has been reconciled or explicitly deferred.
- Duplicate decisions contain content evidence, not just names/dates.
- Both computers can access the intended materials; selected code workflows pass representative execution checks.
- Zotero attachments, Fireflies outputs, and other identified pipelines continue functioning.
- No automation recreates the retired copies during a normal run cycle.
- Recovery restoration is demonstrated for one representative item.
- Updated documentation, manifest, unresolved exceptions and progress log are available in this handoff folder.

## Ongoing upkeep

Use one intake folder, a short weekly filing review, and a documented project closeout step. Keep backups out of everyday project navigation. Use Drive-native shortcuts where a second browsing entry is needed, subject to access checks. Record exceptions rather than forcing all workloads into identical storage behavior.

1	# How to File Things
2	
3	Read this before you put anything on this drive.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Why filing feels hard
8	
9	You have been sorting by subject. Every file has several subjects at once, so
10	several folders are always "correct," and you stall. A finished football GPS
11	report is about football, about GPS, about reporting, and about the 2026 season.
12	Four folders all look right, so it stays in the inbox.
13	
14	The fix is to stop sorting by subject.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## The one principle
19	
20	**The folder answers "what stage is this in." The filename answers "what is it about."**
21	
22	A file has many subjects but only one stage at a time. Stage has exactly one
23	right answer, so there is nothing to decide.
24	
25	Sport, season, vendor, and topic all go in the filename. They are never the
26	reason you pick a folder.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## The ladder
31	
32	Ask these in order. Stop at the first yes. That is the folder.
33	
34	**1. Am I still working on it?**
35	   `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/YYYY-MM-DD_ProjectName/`
36	   Drafts, data pulls, scratch notes, code, half-built decks. If the work is not
37	   done, everything about it lives in the project folder, no matter what type of
38	   file it is.
39	
40	**2. Is it finished, and did I hand it to someone or will I?**
41	   `03_REPORTS/`
42	   The final PDF. The deck you presented. The annual report you submitted. One
43	   file per deliverable. This is the folder you search when someone asks "what
44	   did we send them in October."
45	
46	**3. Is it a blank I reuse to make other things?**
47	   `06_TEMPLATES/`
48	   Empty intake forms, report shells, protocol documents, checklists. If it has
49	   real athlete data in it, it is not a template.
50	
51	**4. Is it about a tool or vendor rather than about athletes?**
52	   `05_SYSTEMS/<Vendor>/`
53	   Contracts, API docs, setup guides, vendor whitepapers, license paperwork.
54	   Catapult, Vald, Hawkin, PFF, Power BI, Claude.
55	
56	**5. Is it standing operational material for one sport and season?**
57	   `02_SPORTS/<Sport>/<Season>/`
58	   Rosters, practice schedules, travel itineraries, team calendars. Only the
59	   recurring stuff you rebuild every season. Not projects, not reports.
60	
61	**6. Is it for my own growth rather than my job's output?**
62	   `09_PRO_DEV/`
63	   Courses, certifications, conference recordings, books, other people's
64	   research papers.
65	
66	**7. Is it administrative?**
67	   `08_ADMIN/`
68	   Meeting notes and transcripts, personnel, policy, equipment, budgets.
69	
70	**8. None of the above, and it is done?**
71	   `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`
72	
73	**Personal, not work?** `11_PERSONAL/` — family, finance, device backups, career
74	   paperwork. Kept out of the work stages, not off the drive.
75	
76	If you get past 8, you did not need the file.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## The hard cases, decided in advance
81	
82	These are the ones that actually stall you. The answers are fixed so you do not
83	have to think about them again.
84	
85	| Thing | Where it goes | Why |
86	|---|---|---|
87	| Annual report, while you are writing it | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | Rung 1 beats rung 2 |
88	| Annual report, the final submitted PDF | `03_REPORTS/` | It shipped |
89	| The eight in-between drafts | Delete, or `_old/` inside the project | Not deliverables |
90	| A deck you built and presented once | `03_REPORTS/` | You handed it to someone |
91	| A deck you present every year to interns | `07_EDUCATION/` | It is curriculum, you reuse it |
92	| CMJ traffic light app code | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | It is a project that happens to be about volleyball |
93	| Volleyball roster for FA2026 | `02_SPORTS/Volleyball/FA2026/` | Standing seasonal material |
94	| Hawkin SaaS agreement | `05_SYSTEMS/Hawkin/` | Vendor paperwork |
95	| A research paper someone else wrote | `09_PRO_DEV/` | Not your output |
96	| A study you are running | `04_RESEARCH/` | Your output, ongoing |
97	| Fireflies transcript of a staff meeting | `08_ADMIN/` | Administrative |
98	| Raw GPS export you pulled for one analysis | Inside that project folder | It belongs to the analysis |
99	| Anything personal | `11_PERSONAL/` | This is Eric's personal Google Drive, not a Baylor account (corrected 2026-10-03) |
100	
101	**The tiebreaker for everything else:** if two rungs both seem right, the lower
102	number wins. The ladder is ordered on purpose.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Naming
107	
108	Three rules. Apply them to new files only. Do not go back and rename 43,000
109	old ones.
110	
111	**1. Date first, if the thing is tied to a moment in time.**
112	   `2026-08-18_` at the front. Year first means it sorts correctly forever.
113	   Use the date it was finished, not the date you last opened it.
114	
115	**2. Subject tag second.**
116	   `FB_`, `VB_`, `WBB_`, `MBB_`, `SOC_`, `SB_`. Season codes are `FA2026`,
117	   `SP2026`, `SUM2026`. Four-digit year, always. Never `FA25`.
118	
119	**3. Underscores, not spaces. No apostrophes. No parentheses.**
120	
121	Put together: `2026-08-18_FB_GPS_WeeklyReport_v2.pdf`
122	
123	**Words that are banned in anything you intend to keep:**
124	`final_final`, `Copy of`, `New`, `Old`, `temp`, `USE THIS`, `v2 (1)`.
125	Every one of those means you already lost track of which copy is current.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Killing redundancy
130	
131	**One home.** A file lives in exactly one folder. If it truly belongs in two,
132	put it in the lower-numbered one and make a Windows shortcut in the other. Never
133	copy.
134	
135	**One current version.** When you save `_v2`, delete `_v1` or move it into an
136	`_old/` folder inside the project. The project folder is allowed to be messy.
137	Nothing above rung 1 is.
138	
139	**When you find three copies of the same file,** keep the one in `03_REPORTS`
140	or `10_ARCHIVE`. Those are the folders that are supposed to be permanent.
141	Delete the rest.
142	
143	**Never keep both the .docx and the .pdf of a finished deliverable in
144	`03_REPORTS`.** Keep the PDF there. The .docx stays with the project.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## The two habits
149	
150	Everything above fails without these. They are the whole system.
151	
152	**1. Friday, 15 minutes: inbox to zero.**
153	Open `00_INBOX`. Run every file down the ladder. File it or delete it. The
154	inbox is a landing strip, not a hangar. Nothing sleeps there over the weekend.
155	
156	**2. When something ships, it moves that day.**
157	The moment you send a report, move the final out of `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` into
158	`03_REPORTS/`, and move the project folder into `_DONE/`. Do it while you still
159	remember which file was the real one. A week later you will not.
160	
161	At year end, `_DONE/` empties into `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`. That takes about ten
162	minutes once a year.
163	
164	---
165	
166	## What "done" looks like
167	
168	- `00_INBOX` is empty most days.
169	- `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE` holds fewer than ten folders. If it holds thirty, most
170	  of them are actually stalled, and they should say so.
171	- You can find any finished deliverable from the last three years by opening
172	  `03_REPORTS` and sorting by name, because the dates are in front.
173	- You never think about where a file goes. You run the ladder and stop at the
174	  first yes.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## The one list (added 2026-10-03)
179	
180	Every project, whether it lives here, in `~/DEV`, or both, has one row in
181	`~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`. That row is the source of truth for its stage:
182	`01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE`, `_DONE` and `_STALLED` follow the registry, not the other way round.
183	
184	- A project folder here should match its row's `drive_folder`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<DEV name>`.
185	- `python ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py crosswalk` lists any project folder here with
186	  no row, and any row pointing at a folder that is gone. `closeout` and the Friday
187	  `weekly-review` run it for you.
188	- Stay at the My Drive root on purpose: `Zotero_PDFs` (Zotero's attachment base path) and
189	  `Fireflies Meetings`. Moving them breaks a pipeline.
190	- Script-written folders (`Backups`, `Cloud_Copy`) live in `My Drive/_MACHINE/` since 2026-10-14.
191	  Do not file documents there. Where every kind of file lives: `~/.claude/STORAGE.md`.
192

several folders are always "correct," and you stall. A finished football GPS
report is about football, about GPS, about reporting, and about the 2026 season.
Four folders all look right, so it stays in the inbox.

The fix is to stop sorting by subject.

---

## The one principle

**The folder answers "what stage is this in." The filename answers "what is it about."**

A file has many subjects but only one stage at a time. Stage has exactly one
right answer, so there is nothing to decide.

Sport, season, vendor, and topic all go in the filename. They are never the
reason you pick a folder.

---

## The ladder

Ask these in order. Stop at the first yes. That is the folder.

**1. Am I still working on it?**
   `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/YYYY-MM-DD_ProjectName/`
   Drafts, data pulls, scratch notes, code, half-built decks. If the work is not
   done, everything about it lives in the project folder, no matter what type of
   file it is.

**2. Is it finished, and did I hand it to someone or will I?**
   `03_REPORTS/`
   The final PDF. The deck you presented. The annual report you submitted. One
   file per deliverable. This is the folder you search when someone asks "what
   did we send them in October."

**3. Is it a blank I reuse to make other things?**
   `06_TEMPLATES/`
   Empty intake forms, report shells, protocol documents, checklists. If it has
   real athlete data in it, it is not a template.

**4. Is it about a tool or vendor rather than about athletes?**
   `05_SYSTEMS/<Vendor>/`
   Contracts, API docs, setup guides, vendor whitepapers, license paperwork.
   Catapult, Vald, Hawkin, PFF, Power BI, Claude.

**5. Is it standing operational material for one sport and season?**
   `02_SPORTS/<Sport>/<Season>/`
   Rosters, practice schedules, travel itineraries, team calendars. Only the
   recurring stuff you rebuild every season. Not projects, not reports.

**6. Is it for my own growth rather than my job's output?**
   `09_PRO_DEV/`
   Courses, certifications, conference recordings, books, other people's
   research papers.

**7. Is it administrative?**
   `08_ADMIN/`
   Meeting notes and transcripts, personnel, policy, equipment, budgets.

**8. None of the above, and it is done?**
   `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`

**Personal, not work?** `11_PERSONAL/` — family, finance, device backups, career
   paperwork. Kept out of the work stages, not off the drive.

If you get past 8, you did not need the file.

---

## The hard cases, decided in advance

These are the ones that actually stall you. The answers are fixed so you do not
have to think about them again.

| Thing | Where it goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Annual report, while you are writing it | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | Rung 1 beats rung 2 |
| Annual report, the final submitted PDF | `03_REPORTS/` | It shipped |
| The eight in-between drafts | Delete, or `_old/` inside the project | Not deliverables |
| A deck you built and presented once | `03_REPORTS/` | You handed it to someone |
| A deck you present every year to interns | `07_EDUCATION/` | It is curriculum, you reuse it |
| CMJ traffic light app code | `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` | It is a project that happens to be about volleyball |
| Volleyball roster for FA2026 | `02_SPORTS/Volleyball/FA2026/` | Standing seasonal material |
| Hawkin SaaS agreement | `05_SYSTEMS/Hawkin/` | Vendor paperwork |
| A research paper someone else wrote | `09_PRO_DEV/` | Not your output |
| A study you are running | `04_RESEARCH/` | Your output, ongoing |
| Fireflies transcript of a staff meeting | `08_ADMIN/` | Administrative |
| Raw GPS export you pulled for one analysis | Inside that project folder | It belongs to the analysis |
| Anything personal | `11_PERSONAL/` | This is Eric's personal Google Drive, not a Baylor account (corrected 2026-10-03) |

**The tiebreaker for everything else:** if two rungs both seem right, the lower
number wins. The ladder is ordered on purpose.

---

## Naming

Three rules. Apply them to new files only. Do not go back and rename 43,000
old ones.

**1. Date first, if the thing is tied to a moment in time.**
   `2026-08-18_` at the front. Year first means it sorts correctly forever.
   Use the date it was finished, not the date you last opened it.

**2. Subject tag second.**
   `FB_`, `VB_`, `WBB_`, `MBB_`, `SOC_`, `SB_`. Season codes are `FA2026`,
   `SP2026`, `SUM2026`. Four-digit year, always. Never `FA25`.

**3. Underscores, not spaces. No apostrophes. No parentheses.**

Put together: `2026-08-18_FB_GPS_WeeklyReport_v2.pdf`

**Words that are banned in anything you intend to keep:**
`final_final`, `Copy of`, `New`, `Old`, `temp`, `USE THIS`, `v2 (1)`.
Every one of those means you already lost track of which copy is current.

---

## Killing redundancy

**One home.** A file lives in exactly one folder. If it truly belongs in two,
put it in the lower-numbered one and make a Windows shortcut in the other. Never
copy.

**One current version.** When you save `_v2`, delete `_v1` or move it into an
`_old/` folder inside the project. The project folder is allowed to be messy.
Nothing above rung 1 is.

**When you find three copies of the same file,** keep the one in `03_REPORTS`
or `10_ARCHIVE`. Those are the folders that are supposed to be permanent.
Delete the rest.

**Never keep both the .docx and the .pdf of a finished deliverable in
`03_REPORTS`.** Keep the PDF there. The .docx stays with the project.

---

## The two habits

Everything above fails without these. They are the whole system.

**1. Friday, 15 minutes: inbox to zero.**
Open `00_INBOX`. Run every file down the ladder. File it or delete it. The
inbox is a landing strip, not a hangar. Nothing sleeps there over the weekend.

**2. When something ships, it moves that day.**
The moment you send a report, move the final out of `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE/` into
`03_REPORTS/`, and move the project folder into `_DONE/`. Do it while you still
remember which file was the real one. A week later you will not.

At year end, `_DONE/` empties into `10_ARCHIVE/YYYY/`. That takes about ten
minutes once a year.

---

## What "done" looks like

- `00_INBOX` is empty most days.
- `01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE` holds fewer than ten folders. If it holds thirty, most
  of them are actually stalled, and they should say so.
- You can find any finished deliverable from the last three years by opening
  `03_REPORTS` and sorting by name, because the dates are in front.
- You never think about where a file goes. You run the ladder and stop at the
  first yes.

---

## The one list (added 2026-10-03)

Every project, whether it lives here, in `~/DEV`, or both, has one row in
`~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`. That row is the source of truth for its stage:
`01_PROJECTS/_ACTIVE`, `_DONE` and `_STALLED` follow the registry, not the other way round.

- A project folder here should match its row's `drive_folder`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<DEV name>`.
- `python ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py crosswalk` lists any project folder here with
  no row, and any row pointing at a folder that is gone. `closeout` and the Friday
  `weekly-review` run it for you.
- Stay at the My Drive root on purpose: `Zotero_PDFs` (Zotero's attachment base path) and
  `Fireflies Meetings`. Moving them breaks a pipeline.
- Script-written folders (`Backups`, `Cloud_Copy`) live in `My Drive/_MACHINE/` since 2026-10-14.
  Do not file documents there. Where every kind of file lives: `~/.claude/STORAGE.md`.
